findings.problem: The headline 'One check bit catches one flip' and the last caption 'Two flips cancel out: missed.' teach 'one flip yes, two flips no'. The lesson rule (a6-parity 'What parity cannot do', and its Detected/Missed question) is: any ODD number of flips is caught (1, 3, 5) and any EVEN number is missed (2, 4, 6). A first-time learner can conclude that three flips slip through. 'Cancel out' is also loose on screen: both flips are 0 -> 1, so the count goes 4 -> 5 -> 6 and never returns to 4; only its parity returns to even.
findings.fix: Keep the picture. Change caption 5 (10.7-12.4) to 'Any even number of flips is missed.' (7 words), or add a small grey tag 'odd: caught, even: missed' under the badge during 11.1-12.4 (the area below y about 480 is free). Optionally retitle 'A parity bit catches odd flips' (two lines still fit) and drop 'cancel out' for 'make it even again'.
findings.evidence: s3@11.9: two red tiles, counter 6 (green), badge 'even: looks fine', caption 'Two flips cancel out: missed.'; headline visible in every s3 still. Lesson js/content/algo/algo-p6-x-02.js step 'What parity cannot do' (caught 1, 3, 5; missed 2, 4, 6). Re-ran in node: frame 10110010 has 4 ones, one flip 5, two flips 6.

findings.problem: Nothing says why the division stops. After step 2 the last row is 0000100: a 1 is still sitting in column 4, and a learner who was just told 'Line the pattern up under the next 1' will ask why the pattern is not lined up again. The lesson gives the stopping rule (a6-crc step 'CRC = long division with XOR': 'shorter than 1101: stop'); caption 4 only names the result. Likewise the 'add 000' tag never says why three zeros (one per generator degree, same lesson step), so 3 check bits looks arbitrary.
findings.fix: Caption 4 (8.0-9.7): 'Fewer than four bits left: that is the remainder.' (8 words), or add a small grey tag 'too short for 1101' next to the remainder tag at about 7.8. For the zeros, extend the tag to 'add 000: one 0 per check bit' (there is room to the left of x 352) or caption 2 'Add one zero per check bit, then divide.'
findings.evidence: s4@7.9: last row 0 0 0 0 [1 0 0], remainder tag, caption window opens at 8.0; s4@4.5 'add 000' tag. Lesson js/content/algo/algo-p6.js step 'CRC = long division with XOR' ('Append zeros first, one per generator degree', and the pre block ending 'shorter than 1101: stop').

findings.problem: Scene 5 shows a clean frame leaving 000 but never says why. A first-time learner cannot tell whether 000 is luck or the rule. The lesson reason (a6-crc step 'Why the receiver can check it': appending the remainder makes the whole frame divide exactly by the generator) is neither on screen nor in a caption, so 'clean' is asserted rather than explained.
findings.fix: Cheapest fix, no re-timing: change the badge's valid text from 'clean' to 'divides exactly' (L5.badge valid:, check it fits the 296 px badge) and keep 'error found'. Alternative: add a caption 'A clean frame divides exactly: 000.' by pushing the two-flip demo back about 0.7 s (the scene has a 1.4 s hold at the end).
findings.evidence: s5@2.4: remainder 000 in green, badge 'clean', caption 'Divide the frame by the same pattern.'. Lesson js/content/algo/algo-p6.js step 'Why the receiver can check it'.

findings.problem: Captions 4 and 5 run ahead of their pictures (house rule: a caption must never run ahead). 'Nearest valid word is 000: fixed.' opens at 9.2, but the repair is the token hopping back at 9.65-10.2 with the green ring at 10.2-10.5; at 9.3 the token still sits above red 010. 'Two flips lead to the wrong word.' opens at 11.8, but the wrong repair is the hop to 111 at 12.05-12.55 with the red ring at 12.55-12.85; at 11.85 the token is still on 011.
findings.fix: Caption 4 -> [9.6, 11.2]; caption 5 -> [12.1, 13.8] (ends before the 14 s cut; 6 words each at about 4 words per second). The decoder tags that popped at 9.0 and 11.75 stay on screen, so nothing is lost.
findings.evidence: s7@9.3 and s7@11.85 (caption fading in, repair not yet shown); LEGS [9.65, 10.2] and [12.05, 12.55], T.ring0 [10.2, 10.5], T.ring1 [12.55, 12.85] in videos/a6/scene-07-distance.js.

findings.problem: Nothing explains why the video moves from the 3-copy cube code to Hamming. Scene 7 ends with 'valid words 3 apart fix one flip' for the code 0 = 000, 1 = 111, so a learner's natural question is 'why not just send everything three times?'. Lesson 6.5 'The price: rate' answers it (3 copies: 1 useful bit in 3, rate 1/3; Hamming(7,4): 4 in 7, rate 4/7) and the storyboard even computes and asserts A6.RATE, but no scene shows it. Also the link that Hamming(7,4)'s 16 valid words are themselves at least 3 apart (lesson 6.7 'Why exactly three parity bits'; I re-ran: minimum distance 3) is never made, so scene 10's 'fixes exactly one error' is not tied back to the distance rule. The lesson words 'codeword' and 'Hamming distance' never appear, so the video does not map onto the lesson vocabulary.
findings.fix: Use the end hold of scene 7 (13.0-14.0, room right of the green rule tag at y about 536) for a grey tag '3 copies: 1 useful bit in 3' from A6.RATE.repeat, and a green tag 'Hamming: 4 useful bits in 7' from A6.RATE.hamming in scene 8 (hold 11.1-12.5 or the legend slot 1.1-4.2). Rename the '3 steps apart' tag to '3 steps apart: distance 3' to give the lesson term once.
findings.evidence: videos/a6/common.js lines 239-253 define and assert A6.RATE; grep of videos/a6/scene-*.js finds no use. s7@13.5 end state has no cost information. Lesson js/content/algo/algo-p6-x-03.js step 'The price: rate'.

findings.problem: Two claims are true but not traceable. (1) The tag '16 check bits: every burst up to 16' has no source on screen (the frame has 7 bits; CRC-16 is only in lesson 6.4). (2) Caption 'Even two flips change the remainder.' is true for this 7-bit frame (21 of 21 double flips, asserted) but lesson 6.4's audit shows a degree-3 generator can miss a few double flips on longer frames, so a learner may over-generalise.
findings.fix: Relabel the second tag 'CRC-16: every burst up to 16' (28 characters, still fits) so the learner can find it. Caption 2: 'Even these two flips change the remainder.'
findings.evidence: s5@10.5 (both rule tags), s5@5.0 (caption 2). Node re-run: 7/7 singles, 21/21 doubles, 23/23 bursts, but only 28/35 triples caught for 1101 on 7 bits. Lesson js/content/algo/algo-p6-x-02.js step 'What a good generator catches' and predict a6-crcpoly-2.

Until 8.3 only the 'minutes away' tag and the dotted wire support it. Caption 4 'So it must repair errors itself.' opens at 9.5, just before the repair at 9.6-10.05.

findings.evidence: s6@7.5 (caption says cannot wait, return arrow not started), s6@9.3 ('too slow' tag and stalled arrow). Timings T.bAsk.arrow [8.3, 9.4], T.bAsk.slow [9.2, 9.55].

findings.problem: Lesson a6-crc step 'Why the receiver can check it' says 'A good generator catches every single-bit error, every burst shorter than its degree'. Lesson 6.4, the bank (js/bank/algo-32.js, algo-33.js) and the video (scene 5 tag '3 check bits: every burst up to 3') all say up to and including the degree, which is the correct maths (a generator of degree r with a 1 in its last place catches every burst of length r or less). The video is right; the 6.3 sentence is off by one.
findings.fix: Lesson fix only: change 'shorter than its degree' to 'up to its degree' in js/content/algo/algo-p6.js (step 'Why the receiver can check it'). No video change.
findings.evidence: js/content/algo/algo-p6.js line 60; js/content/algo/algo-p6-x-02.js 'What a good generator catches'; node audit: 23 of 23 bursts of up to 3 bits caught by 1101.

findings.problem: Lesson a6-hamming step 'The limit: one error' says 'A plain Hamming code can notice that something is wrong with two errors, but cannot repair them.' That contradicts the same lesson's predict a6-ham-1 ('nothing warns the receiver'), its 'Try every error' callout ('The decoder never notices') and the video, where after the wrong 'repair' all three checks pass (scene 10: 0010110 is itself a valid codeword with data 1110). The video is right; a decoder that applies the usual fix cannot tell two flips from one. Only distance-3 detection without correction, or SECDED, can flag them.
findings.fix: Lesson fix only: reword to 'With two errors a plain Hamming decoder cannot even tell: after its fix every check passes. An extra overall parity bit (SECDED) lets you detect double errors.' in js/content/algo/algo-p6-x-04.js. No video change.
findings.evidence: js/content/algo/algo-p6-x-04.js line 359 versus predict a6-ham-1 in js/content/algo/algo-p6.js ('nothing warns the receiver'), predict a6-ham-2 and the 'Try every error' callout in algo-p6-x-04.js; s10@9.6 (all ticks green, data 1110). Node: 0 of 336 double flips repaired, and the 'repaired' word passes every check.

findings.problem: videos/_plan/algo-6.json recap row 1 still describes 'a strip of five bit tiles (bits 10110 ... last tile orange)'. As an even-parity frame that is wrong: message 1011 has three 1s, so its parity bit is 1 (10111). The scene file correctly draws 10111 plus the CRC frame 1011100 and asserts it, so the video is right; the storyboard is stale and would reintroduce the error if the scene were regenerated from it.
findings.fix: Update the recap pictogram text in algo-6.json to '10111' and mention the second strip (CRC frame 1011100) that the scene now draws.
findings.evidence: algo-6.json recap points[0].pictogram vs videos/a6/scene-11-recap.js lines 41-47 (A6.same 'recap row 1: parity frame', '10111'); s11@8.5 shows 1 1 1 1 1 and 1 1 1 1 1 0 0.

findings.problem: The call to action 'Next: Workshop 6.W' is out of order in the app: the workshop is order 90, the boss 99 and the recap video 100 (js/content/algo/videos.js 'after the boss quiz'), so a learner watching the video in the path has already done the workshop. The same wording is used by the finished a4, a5 and l5 videos, so this is a series-wide convention rather than an a6 defect.
findings.fix: Decide once for the series: either keep it (video also works as a standalone primer) or use wording that is true in either position, e.g. 'Try it: Workshop 6.W'. If changed, change it in the recap of every phase together.
